$comment: Two kinds, and the distinction is the point. `wcag-exempt` means the
success criterion does not apply — the pairing is correct and will never
need fixing. `defect` means it genuinely fails and is not fixed yet; the
gate keeps reporting those in its summary so they cannot be forgotten,
and they are copied into every affected component's contract as
a11y.knownIssues so a consumer is told before they ship it.
An exception that no longer fails is itself an error. Otherwise this file
$deferredModesComment: Dark is DEFERRED, not exempt and not passing.
The dark theme has not been finalised in Figma yet. Measuring a theme that is
still being designed produces findings that are true of today's values and
meaningless as decisions — and worse, they were being shipped: all three
outstanding defects were Dark, they were written into Button and Alert's
a11y.knownIssues on npm, and ionbase-ui/eslint-plugin was telling consumers
not to use `variant="primary-soft"` on the strength of them. A light-only app
was being warned off a component that is fine.
While a mode is deferred the gate still MEASURES it and still prints the
results, so nothing is lost or hidden. It just does not fail the build, does
not enter any component contract, and is not linted.
Remove 'Dark' from this list once the dark theme is settled in Figma. Every
deferred result becomes a real finding again the moment you do.
HOW MANY, is a question for the gate and not for this comment. This text used
to answer it — 'on today's values that is 3 defects' — and by 3 Sep 2026 it was
8, because the agentic tier shipped and nobody edits a sentence to match a
measurement. The count now comes from the measurement: `pnpm --filter ionbase-ui
contrast` prints every deferred pairing, flags the ones already exempt, and ends
with 'N without an exemption'. The entries below are the SUBSET that has been
investigated and written up, not the whole list.
Four of the unexempt eight are the same empty-element false positives already
exempted under Light — the confidence bars and the streaming cursor, neither of
which holds text. They are deliberately NOT given Dark exemptions here, because
an exemption cites a measured ratio and measuring a theme still being designed
produces a number that is true today and meaningless as a decision. Write them
when Dark is final, with real values.

accepted.reason: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component: it has no contrast requirement. Disabled controls are required to look unavailable, and raising this would work against that.

Not a text pairing. `.ion-confidence__bar--on` is an empty, aria-hidden <span> — the gate pairs the inherited text colour against its background because it models every element as potentially holding text. There is no text here and SC 1.4.3 does not apply. What DOES apply is SC 1.4.11, and it was measured by hand: the filled bar reads 5.32:1 against the unfilled one, and the unfilled bar's outline reads 7.09:1 against the page. Both clear 3:1.
As above — an empty bar, not text. Filled vs unfilled measures 6.65:1, over the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 asks of a non-text indicator.
As above — an empty bar, not text. Filled vs unfilled measures 4.67:1, over 3:1.

Not a text pairing. `.ion-streaming-text__cursor` is an empty, aria-hidden <span> drawn as a block — deliberately not a text character, since some screen readers read a literal cursor glyph aloud. The gate pairs the paragraph's inherited colour against the cursor's background. Measured properly, the cursor is 7.09:1 against the page.

The same SC 1.4.3 exemption as --text-disabled on --surface-disabled, reached from the other direction. A disabled label declares a colour and no background of its own, so from 3 Sep 2026 it is measured against the three neutral grounds it could sit on. Muted is the darkest of them and the only one it falls short against. The criterion exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component regardless of what is behind it, and raising this would work against the requirement that disabled controls look unavailable.

deferred.reason: Same exemption as Light — SC 1.4.3 incidental text, inactive component.

Long-recorded. Fix is the same shape as the success green on 2026-08-18: move the PURPLE PRIMITIVES, not the role binding. Re-pointing surface/information at information/700 would make the base identical to its own hover.
deferred.note: AGENTS.md described this role as 'not yet used'. That was wrong, and this gate is what proved it — Alert ships it today.

deferred.reason: Found by this gate on 2026-08-18, not previously known. Button primary-soft on hover in dark mode. Marginal — 4.25 against 4.5 — but it is an interactive state, so it is the state a user is most likely to be reading when they act.
Same pair of values as the hover case above — surface/primary-tint and surface/primary-subtle/hover both resolve to #0e2d8b in Dark. One fix addresses both.

Citation on a hovered primary-subtle surface. The THIRD component to land on #0e2d8b in Dark — surface/primary-tint and surface/primary-subtle/hover both resolve to it, and text/link and text/primary both read 4.25:1 against it. One primitive shift fixes all three. Undocumented until 3 Sep 2026, when the gate was made to count its own deferred findings instead of a comment claiming there were three.
SC 1.4.3 incidental text, inactive component — the same categorical exemption as Light. Listed per ground because a disabled label declares no background of its own and is measured against all three.
